```{r}
#2021 gap by age
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)

# 'data' is your 2021 cleaned dataset already in memory:
# data <- arrow::read_parquet("/Users/hxw/sta313A2/data/01-cleaned_data/cleaned_census_data.parquet")

# Map census AGEGRP codes to labels
age_labels <- c(
  `7` = "18–19",
  `8` = "20–24",
  `9` = "25–29",
  `10` = "30–34",
  `11` = "35–39",
  `12` = "40–44",
  `13` = "45–49",
  `14` = "50–54",
  `15` = "55–59",
  `16` = "60–64"
)

# Prep 2021 data
df21 <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = recode(as.character(Gender), `1` = "Women", `2` = "Men"),
    Age = recode(as.character(AGEGRP), !!!age_labels)
  ) %>%
  filter(Gender %in% c("Women", "Men"), !is.na(Wages), !is.na(Age))

# Compute gap by age for 2021: Gap = (Men − Women) / Men using medians
gap_age <- df21 %>%
  group_by(Age, Gender) %>%
  summarise(med = median(Wages, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Gender, values_from = med) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Men), !is.na(Women)) %>%
  mutate(Age = factor(Age, levels = age_labels),
         gap_pct = (Men - Women) / Men) %>%
  arrange(Age)

# Red highlight point at 25–29
pts_2529     <- gap_age %>% filter(Age == "25–29")
pt_2529_top  <- pts_2529  # used for the ggrepel note

p_2021 <- ggplot(gap_age, aes(Age, gap_pct, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, color = "black") +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "black") +
  # red dot + label at 25–29
  geom_point(
    data = pts_2529,
    aes(Age, gap_pct),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.8,
    color = "red"
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = pts_2529,
    aes(Age, gap_pct, label = "Mean maternal \nage in Canada)"),
    color = "red",
    segment.color = "red",
    nudge_y = 0.06,
    box.padding = 0.35,
    size = 3.2,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  # Y axis: 0–30%
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 0.30),
    breaks = seq(0, 0.30, by = 0.05),
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Canada’s gender pay gap by age (2021)",
    x = "Age group",
    y = "Gap percentage",
    caption = "Figure shows the gender pay gap by age for full-time, full-year workers. The gap narrows in the \nearly 20s, then rises sharply from 25–30 and continues to increase steadily thereafter."
    
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    # center the title
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 9.5,
      colour = "#5a5a5a",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(t = 10)
    )
  )


p_2021
```

```{r}
# gap by education
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Compute median wages by Education × Gender, then the gap = (Men − Women) / Men
edu_gap <- clean_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Edu3)) %>%
  group_by(Edu3, Gender) %>%
  summarise(med_wage = median(Wages, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gender, values_from = med_wage) %>%
  mutate(gap_pct = (Men - Women) / Men) %>%
  drop_na(gap_pct) %>%
  # order categories from lowest → highest gap
  mutate(Edu3 = as.character(Edu3)) %>%
  arrange(gap_pct) %>%
  mutate(Edu3 = factor(Edu3, levels = Edu3))

# palette per education level (tweak if you like)
edu_cols <- c(
  "HS or less"          = "#fdbb84",
  "Non-degree postsec"  = "#9ecae1",
  "BA or higher"        = "#a1d99b"
)

ggplot(edu_gap, aes(x = gap_pct, y = Edu3, fill = Edu3)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(gap_pct, accuracy = 0.1)),
            hjust = -0.12, size = 3.2, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = edu_cols, name = "Education") +
  labs(
    title   = "Gender pay gap by education level",
    x       = "Gap percentage",
    y       = NULL,
    caption = "Figure shows the gender pay gap by education level. The gap is largest among those with non-degree postsecondary \ncredentials (25.3%) and smallest among those with a bachelor’s degree or higher (16.8%)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "right",
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.caption        = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

```{r}
  `91` = "Public administration"

naics_gap <- clean_data %>%
  mutate(NAICS_lab = recode(as.character(NAICS), !!!naics_labs)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(NAICS_lab)) %>%
  group_by(NAICS_lab, Gender) %>%
  summarise(med_wage = median(Wages, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gender, values_from = med_wage) %>%
  mutate(
    gap_pct = (Men - Women) / Men,
    # (Men − Women) / Men
    gap_cat = case_when(
      gap_pct < 0    ~ "Women higher",
      gap_pct < 0.10 ~ "0–10%",
      gap_pct < 0.20 ~ "10–20%",
      TRUE           ~ "≥20%"
    ),
    # set factor order HIGH → LOW so bars run top (largest) to bottom (smallest) after coord_flip()
    NAICS_lab = fct_reorder(NAICS_lab, gap_pct, .desc = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(gap_pct)

# palette with strong separation (green for negative, oranges/reds for larger gaps)
pal <- c(
  "Women higher" = "#2ca25f",
  "0–10%"       = "#fee8c8",
  "10–20%"      = "#fdbb84",
  "≥20%"        = "#e34a33"
)

# --- single plot object ---
p_naics <- ggplot(naics_gap, aes(
  x = reorder(NAICS_lab, gap_pct),
  y = gap_pct,
  fill = gap_cat
)) +
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(grid)

# ---------- helpers ----------
who_lab <- function(gender, kids) {
  paste0(ifelse(gender == "Men", "men", "women"),
         "\n",
         ifelse(kids == "Has children", "with\nchildren", "without\nchildren"))
}

# Use the pts you already have, but DROP the "Men — No children" point,
# because that dot is drawn from baseline_dots at x = 0 (to avoid duplicate labels).
pts_nonbase <- pts %>%
  filter(!(Gender == "Men" & ChildStatus == "No children"))

# Build the % labels that sit UNDER each dot (colored like the dot)
pct_labels <- bind_rows(
  # real (non-baseline) dots: men-with-children, women-with/without
  pts_nonbase %>%
    transmute(
      x      = gap +
        case_when(
          Gender == "Women" & ChildStatus == "Has children"  ~ -0.010, # separate the two red dots
          Gender == "Women" & ChildStatus == "No children"   ~  0.010,
          TRUE                                                ~  0
        ),
      y      = line_y - 0.08,
      lab    = percent(gap, accuracy = 0.1),
      col    = dot_col
    ),
  # baseline 0% labels (only once per line, from baseline_dots)
  baseline_dots %>%
    transmute(
      x   = gap,
      y   = line_y - 0.08,
      lab = percent(0, accuracy = 0.1),
      col = dot_col
    )
)

# Build the “who” labels under the percent labels (also colored like the dot)
who_labels <- bind_rows(
  pts_nonbase %>%
    transmute(
      x = gap +
        case_when(
          Gender == "Women" & ChildStatus == "Has children"  ~ -0.010,
          Gender == "Women" & ChildStatus == "No children"   ~  0.010,
          TRUE                                                ~  0
        ),
      y   = line_y - 0.27,                 # sit a bit lower than the % text
      lab = who_lab(Gender, ChildStatus),
      col = dot_col
    ),
  baseline_dots %>%
    transmute(
      x   = 0,
      y   = line_y - 0.27,
      lab = "men\nwithout\nchildren",       # baseline label appears once per line
      col = "#4F83FF"
    )
)

# ---------- plot ----------
ggplot() +
  # number lines with double arrows
  geom_segment(aes(x = x_left, xend = x_right, y = 1, yend = 1),
               linewidth = 1.1, color = "grey35",
               arrow = arrow(ends = "both", type = "closed", length = unit(6, "pt"))) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x_left, xend = x_right, y = 0, yend = 0),
               linewidth = 1.1, color = "grey35",
               arrow = arrow(ends = "both", type = "closed", length = unit(6, "pt"))) +
  # center tick (0%) on both lines
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = -0.06, yend = 0.06),
               color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # baseline blue dots at 0% (both lines)
  geom_point(data = baseline_dots,
             aes(x = gap, y = line_y),
             color = baseline_dots$dot_col, size = baseline_dots$dot_size) +
  # group dots (no double-draw of men-no-children)
  geom_point(data = pts_nonbase,
             aes(x = gap, y = line_y),
             color = pts_nonbase$dot_col, size = pts_nonbase$dot_size) +
  # percent labels (under dots)
  geom_text(data = pct_labels,
            aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab, colour = I(col)),
            size = 3.3, vjust = 1) +
  # who labels (beneath the percents)
  geom_text(data = who_labels,
            aes(x = x, y = y, label = lab, colour = I(col)),
            lineheight = 1.05, size = 3.3) +
  # Less / More at line ends
  annotate("text", x = x_left,  y = 1, label = "Less",  hjust = 1.1, vjust = 0.5, size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = 1, label = "More",  hjust = -0.1, vjust = 0.5, size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = x_left,  y = 0, label = "Less",  hjust = 1.1, vjust = 0.5, size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = 0, label = "More",  hjust = -0.1, vjust = 0.5, size = 4) +
  # “Wage gap” centered above each line
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 1.12, label = "Wage gap", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.12, label = "Wage gap", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  # axis / view
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(x_left, x_right), ylim = c(-0.45, 1.35), clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "How parenthood shapes the gender wage gap relative to men without children (ages 25–44)?",
    caption = "Top line: wage gaps for men (with vs. without children); bottom line: wage gaps for women relative to men without \nchildren. Parenthood is associated with a wage premium for men and a pronounced penalty for women—largest \nfor women with children.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid      = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y     = element_blank(),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 10.2),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.margin     = margin(t = 8, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10)
  )
```

```{r}
# --- Parent premium/penalty on a single number line --------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(grid)

# Build the four groups (ages 25–44, full-time/full-year already in clean_data)
pts <- clean_data %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = recode(as.character(Gender), `1`="Women", `2`="Men"),
    ChildStatus = case_when(PKIDS == 1 ~ "Has children",
                            PKIDS == 0 ~ "No children",
                            TRUE ~ NA_character_)
  ) %>%
  filter(AGEGRP %in% 9:12,                      # 25–44
         Gender %in% c("Men","Women"),
         !is.na(ChildStatus),
         !is.na(Wages)) %>%
  group_by(Gender, ChildStatus) %>%
  summarise(med = median(Wages, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # baseline = Men — No children
  mutate(baseline = med[Gender == "Men" & ChildStatus == "No children"][1],
         gap = (med - baseline) / baseline) %>%
  mutate(
    # aesthetics for the four dots
    dot_col = case_when(
      Gender == "Men"    & ChildStatus == "No children" ~ "#4F83FF", # blue (baseline)
      Gender == "Men"    & ChildStatus == "Has children" ~ "#2E5BD4", # darker blue
      Gender == "Women"  & ChildStatus == "No children" ~ "#F48FB1", # pink
      Gender == "Women"  & ChildStatus == "Has children" ~ "#E53935"  # red
    ),
    who = paste(if_else(Gender=="Men","men","women"),
                if_else(ChildStatus=="Has children","\nwith\nchildren","\nwithout\nchildren")),
    # --- NEW: small horizontal nudge so the two women's labels don't overlap ---
    x_nudge = case_when(
      Gender == "Women" & ChildStatus == "Has children"  ~ -0.012, # move a bit left
      Gender == "Women" & ChildStatus == "No children"   ~  0.012, # move a bit right
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )

# handy values for brackets
g_men_nc  <- pts$gap[pts$Gender=="Men"   & pts$ChildStatus=="No children"]
g_men_wc  <- pts$gap[pts$Gender=="Men"   & pts$ChildStatus=="Has children"]
g_wom_nc  <- pts$gap[pts$Gender=="Women" & pts$ChildStatus=="No children"]
g_wom_wc  <- pts$gap[pts$Gender=="Women" & pts$ChildStatus=="Has children"]

# differences to show above brackets
delta_womNC_menNC <- g_men_nc - g_wom_nc
delta_womWC_menWC <- g_men_wc - g_wom_wc

# number-line limits
x_left  <- -0.20
x_right <-  0.20

# y positions
y_line  <- 0
y_pct   <- -0.03     # percent just under each dot
y_who   <- -0.10     # two-line labels under the percent
y_brk1  <-  0.12     # small bracket height
y_brk2  <-  0.20     # big bracket height

# a small helper to draw squared brackets
bracket <- function(x0, x1, y, tick = 0.03, ...) {
  list(
    annotate("segment", x = x0, xend = x0, y = y, yend = y - tick, ...),
    annotate("segment", x = x0, xend = x1, y = y, yend = y, ...),
    annotate("segment", x = x1, xend = x1, y = y, yend = y - tick, ...)
  )
}

# Plot
ggplot() +
  # arrowed number line
  geom_segment(aes(x = x_left, xend = x_right, y = y_line, yend = y_line),
               linewidth = 1.2, color = "grey30",
               arrow = arrow(ends = "both", type = "closed", length = unit(6, "pt"))) +
  annotate("text", x = x_left,  y = y_line, label = "Less",  hjust = 1.2, vjust = 0.4, size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = y_line, label = "More",  hjust = -0.2, vjust = 0.4, size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = y_line - 0.185, label = "Wage comparing to man without children", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  # zero tick
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = y_line - 0.04, yend = y_line + 0.04),
               color = "grey45", linewidth = 0.6) +
  # the four dots
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x = gap, y = y_line), color = pts$dot_col, size = 4) +
  # % under each dot (colored like the dot) — now use x = gap + x_nudge
  geom_text(data = pts,
            aes(x = gap + x_nudge, y = y_pct, label = percent(gap, accuracy = 0.1),
                colour = I(dot_col)),
            size = 3, vjust = 1) +
  # who-labels under the % — now use x = gap + x_nudge
  geom_text(data = pts,
            aes(x = gap + x_nudge, y = y_who, label = who, colour = I(dot_col)),
            lineheight = 0.95, size = 3) +

  # ---- Brackets like your sketch ----
  # small bracket: women w/o children  → men w/o children (≈ 13.9%)
  bracket(g_wom_nc, g_men_nc, y = y_brk1, color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.7)+
  annotate("text", x = (g_wom_nc + g_men_nc)/2, y = y_brk1 + 0.03,
           label = percent(delta_womNC_menNC, accuracy = 0.1), size = 4)+
  # big bracket: women w/ children → men w/ children (≈ 22.2%)
  bracket(g_wom_wc, g_men_wc, y = y_brk2, color = "black", linewidth = 0.7)+
  annotate("text", x = (g_wom_wc + g_men_wc)/2, y = y_brk2 + 0.03,
           label = percent(delta_womWC_menWC, accuracy = 0.1), size = 4)+

  # axis & theme
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 10),
                     breaks = seq(-0.2, 0.2, by = 0.1)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(x_left, x_right), ylim = c(-0.26, 0.28), clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "How parenthood shapes the gender wage gap relative to men without children\n(ages 25–44)",
    caption = "Top line: wage gaps for men (with vs. without children); bottom line: wage gaps for women relative to men without \nchildren. Parenthood is associated with a wage premium for men and a pronounced penalty for women—largest \nfor women with children.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 6, r = 12, b = 8, l = 12),
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(size = 10.2),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0),
  )
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

## 1) Prep from `another`
lf <- another %>%
  # keep only the labour force rows (your file is already filtered, but this is harmless)
  filter(Employment_status %in% c("Employed", "Unemployed")) %>%
  select(Age, Gender, Unemployed)

## 2) Unemployment rate by age × gender
age_gender_rate <- lf %>%
  group_by(Age, Gender) %>%
  summarise(
    unemployed = sum(Unemployed, na.rm = TRUE),
    labour     = n(),
    rate       = unemployed / labour,
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

## 3) Plot — Men blue, Women red
ggplot(age_gender_rate,
       aes(x = Age, y = rate, group = Gender, color = Gender)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.05) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Men" = "#4F83FF", "Women" = "#E15759")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment rate by age",
    subtitle = "Among the labour force (employed + unemployed), ages 25–64",
    x = "Age group",
    y = "Unemployment rate",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position   = "top",
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank()
  )

```


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# Expecting clean_unemp with columns:
# Age (factor), Gender ("Women"/"Men"), Employment_status, Unemployed (logical), ChildStatus ("Has children"/"No children")
# If you loaded it as `another`, just do: clean_unemp <- another

# Keep women in the labour force (your file already filtered to InLF, but this is harmless)
lf_women <- another %>%
  filter(Gender == "Women",
         Employment_status %in% c("Employed","Unemployed"),
         !is.na(ChildStatus))

# Unemployment rate by Age × ChildStatus
urate_women_age <- lf_women %>%
  group_by(Age, ChildStatus) %>%
  summarise(
    labour = n(),
    urate  = mean(Unemployed, na.rm = TRUE),   # Unemployed / (Employed + Unemployed)
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot: Has children = red, No children = pink
ggplot(urate_women_age, aes(x = Age, y = urate, color = ChildStatus, group = ChildStatus)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Has children" = "#E53935",  # red
                                "No children" = "#F48FB1")) + # pink  ← plus goes here
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment rate by age among women: with vs. without children",
    subtitle = "Rate = Unemployed / (Employed + Unemployed) within each age group",
    x = "Age group", y = "Unemployment rate", color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
